title: Night briefing — staggered launch playbook
content:
Context:
- This is a lightweight night-run checklist for a staggered model flip (hosted + dedicated slices). Goal: minimize customer disruption during a minor inference runtime rollout that touches KV cache handling and a quantization runtime tweak.
- Target window: 02:00–04:30 UTC (low traffic across NA/EU). Primary risk: memory pressure + tail latency increase under long-seq demos. Secondary risk: tenant cold starts.
- Owners: me (Ellie) = lead; on-call SRE = Akash; PM = Marina.

High-level plan (timeline):
- T-60m: preflight checks and communication
  - Post short note to #deploys + page on-call with TL; include expected traffic deltas and rollback criteria.
  - Run quick health baseline: 15m p95/p99, error-rate, GPU memory headroom per pool. Record snapshots (SLO-BASELINE-TS).
  - Lock CI -> prevent hot PR merges for runtime/serving for the window.

- T-30m: warmup + synthetic litmus
  - Start synthetic workload against a shadow fleet replicating 5% of normal rps (use load script: infra/tools/night-lt.sh).
  - Verify KV cache hit ratios are stable. Look for >80% prefix hits for repeated prompt set.
  - Run stress on long-sequence path (token length 2k) to validate memory usage.

- T=0: cohort 0 (internal + dev clients) -> 0.5% traffic for 15m
  - Route flag: featureFlag:staged_model_flip = cohort-0
  - Metrics to watch: p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, 95th token CPU/GPU utilization, GPU mem RSS, OOMs, asg queue depth.
  - Safety gates: abort if p99 increases >25% from baseline OR error-rate increases >0.5pp absolute OR any OOMs.

- T+15m: cohort 1 -> 2% traffic for 20m (small external beta tenants)
  - If cohort 0 is green, bump routing to cohort-1.
  - Add tenant-allowlist for high-risk accounts to remain on previous variant for now.
  - Verify telemetry: sampling traces for 5 traffic routes.

- T+35m: cohort 2 -> 10% for 30m (regional slices, NA small tenants)
  - Autoscale pools active; monitor queue occupancy and request backlog.
  - Trigger cache warmup jobs for high-volume tenants via admin cron. Monitor for cache thrash.

- T+65m: cohort 3 -> 30% for 30m (wider rollout)
  - At this stage watch for slow drift in p99 and embed-cost changes (token-per-response).

- T+95m: full open -> 100% if all OK; otherwise hold and run deeper diagnostics

Quick commands (ops shortcuts):
- Rollback routing -> /ops/route set featureFlag:staged_model_flip=off (immediate)
- Pin a tenant to old model -> admin/tenant-pin --tenant=<id> --model=runtime-v17
- Force-dequeue warmup -> infra/warmup kick --tenant=<id>
- Kick synthetic monitor -> infra/monitor run night-lt --suite=long-seq

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Immediate rollback if any of:
  - Any OOM observed on serving instances
  - p99 > baseline * 1.25 sustained for 10m
  - Error-rate (5m rolling) increases by >0.5 percentage points
  - Cascade of retries observed (client-side 429s spike >2x baseline)

Post-rollback triage steps:
- Flip routing off (command above); notify #deploys and on-call.
- Snapshot heap/proc stats and orchestrator logs for 30m window.
- Collect sample requests that saw errors (trace ids) and push to /tmp/release-failures-<ts>.tar.gz.
- Triage runbook: assign SRE + model team + infra lead and open JIRA with initial tag release-failure-night.

Version pinning notes (short):
- Preferred flow: admin/tenant-pin tool (safe, persists across restarts).
- For emergency temporary pin: set routing override with TTL of 2h so it auto-expires. Use: admin/route-override --tenant=<id> --model=runtime-v16 --ttl=120m
- Add note in ticket JIRA-4218 with tenant IDs pinned and reason.

Observability checklist (what to watch in dashboards):
- Telemetry: latency (p50/p95/p99), request-size distribution, model token emission variance.
- Cost signals: GPU token-rate, mem-alloc rate.
- Error channels: client 4xx/5xx, internal 5xx, model rejection/error payloads.
- Business signals: chat throughput for paying tenants, embedding queue fullness.

Special tenant considerations:
- VIP tenant X (id: t-7883): keep pinned to runtime-v16 until cohort 3 green. Notify their CSM proactively.
- Experimental tenant pool: allow opt-in test via SSO flag; collect qualitative feedback directly.

Open questions / TODO before launch:
- Q1: Can we reduce warmup time for tiny tenants with cold caches? (Akash)
- Q2: Do we have a smoke test that simulates long-seq maintainable memory pattern across GPUs? If not, add one (owner: Ellie).
- TODO: Add automated post-rollout compare job to run A/B on random sample (create infra job).
- TODO: Draft short customer note for potential latency blips (CS owns).

Notes & heuristics (ops intuition):
- Conservative hold times help detect slow accumulative regressions; prefer 20–30m holds on early cohorts.
- When memory headroom is low, small increases in token length often cascade to OOMs; artificially cap max seq length in canary traffic to reduce noise.
- If we see backend retries from SDKs, prioritize rollback — retries usually amplify the problem.

Contact list for the window:
- On-call SRE: Akash Patel (slack @akash, pager)
- Infra lead: Jordan Li (slack @jordli)
- Model owner: Marina Gomez (slack @marina)
- PM: Theo Barnes (slack @theob)
- CS escalation: Priya Shah (slack @priyash)

Final quick checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] Post note to #deploys + tag on-call
- [ ] Snapshot baseline metrics (attach to ticket)
- [ ] Lock CI merges for serving/runtime repos
- [ ] Start synthetic litmus and verify warmup
- [ ] Confirm command access with SRE (ops admin keys present)
- [ ] Prepare rollback ticket template and assign reviewers

End-of-run: postmortem template (fill within 24h):
- Short summary of rollout and outcome
- Key signals that led to success/failure
- Timeline of actions and who did what
- Follow-ups (who, what, when)
- Retrospective: how to make next run safer/faster

-- end of scratchpad --
